review_notes:
I read all 172 lines: the definition `cavityGroupLift`, its support, gram, restrict and projection lemmas, `cavityNormalizeFrame_spectral_support`, `cavity_complement_projection`, `cavityRetainedFrame_exists`, and the three closing support/projector lemmas. I checked the Mathlib definitions of `Matrix.diagonal_apply`, `Matrix.diagonal_apply_eq` and `Matrix.diagonal_apply_ne` in Mathlib/Data/Matrix/Diagonal.lean. I also searched for a Mathlib lemma that turns a finite sum of diagonal matrices into one diagonal matrix, which could shorten `cavitySpectralProjectors_sum`, but found only a tsum version in Topology/Instances/Matrix.lean, so I did not flag that proof.

Most proofs are already short and clear. The `Finset.sum_congr_set` / `Equiv.sum_comp` calc, the fromCols/fromRows argument and the existence proof all spell out the mathematical idea directly. I did not report changes like turning `hBY` into a `transpose_eq_zero` rewrite, because they would only be a matter of taste.

There is one finding: an unnecessary case split in the last branch of `cavityGroupLift_projection`. The replacement has not been compiled. It only uses `simp only` lemmas that this file already uses (`Matrix.diagonal_apply`, `ite_false`) plus core's `ite_self`. The main uncertainty is that the second `simp only` might need `if_false` instead of `ite_false`, but `ite_false` already works with this toolchain at lines 61 and 102.

findings.excerpt:
by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst j
      simp only [Matrix.diagonal_apply_eq, hi, ite_false]
    · rw [Matrix.diagonal_apply_ne _ hij]
findings.problem: In the last case (`g i ≠ a`, `g j ≠ a`), the left side has already been simplified to `0`. The right side is `diagonal (fun i => if g i = a then 1 else 0) i j`, which is zero for both `i = j` and `i ≠ j`: if `i = j`, the entry is `if g i = a then 1 else 0 = 0` by `hi`. The extra `by_cases hij : i = j`, `subst`, and the two different diagonal lemmas (`diagonal_apply_eq` and `diagonal_apply_ne`) only re-prove that both branches of the diagonal's `if` are zero.
findings.proposed_change:
Unfold the diagonal entry with `Matrix.diagonal_apply` and let `hi` and `ite_self` close it in the same simp call, so the nested split is removed:
```lean
  · simp only [Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply,
      cavityGroupLift, hi, hj, dite_false, zero_mul, Finset.sum_const_zero, add_zero,
      Matrix.diagonal_apply, ite_false, ite_self]
```
If the single combined call doesn't fire in this order, a safe fallback is to keep the existing first `simp only` and replace lines 100–103 with `simp only [Matrix.diagonal_apply, hi, ite_false, ite_self]`.
findings.benefit: This removes a nested case split and one `subst`. The branch then reads as one idea: both lifted factors vanish off group `a`, and the projector entry is `0` because its indicator `if g i = a then 1 else 0` is `0`. `Matrix.diagonal_apply` already appears in the first branch's simp set (line 89), so the four branches use the diagonal more consistently.

evidence.excerpt: theorem diagonal_apply [Zero α] (d : n → α) (i j) : diagonal d i j = if i = j then d i else 0 :=
Matrix.diagonal (fun i => if g i = a then (1 : ℝ) else 0) := by
